lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pronunciation of the -ing and -ed feeling words. Practise allows students to listen and repeat the feeling words in a structured question and answer.
Look for careful listening, clear pronunciation and repetition of the target words, accurate sound-image recognition, and confident pronunciation of both -ing and -ed feeling words.

“Do you remember my favourite thing at the amusement park? That’s right, it was the haunted house! It was scary - I was really scared! What was your favourite thing? How did you feel? Let’s listen to the children talking about how they feel.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives controlled speaking practise with -ing and -ed feeling words prompting students to form questions and short replies from the visuals, showing they can use the target feeling words accurately in conversation.
Look for clear questions and answers, accurate references to the pictures, and both partners taking turns to ask and answer.
“I want to know all about your day at the amusement park! How was the parade? And the roller coaster? Amy, Nick, Minh and Tim went to an amusement park too. Let’s find out how they felt!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Solve and write the letters

details: Solve and write the letters reviews and reinforces the target feelings words using a simple code puzzle.
Look for correctly spelled adjectives accurately matched to their corresponding pictures, neat handwriting, sounding out of words as they write.

“You know I really love puzzles, and secret codes. Can you help me solve this puzzle? Let's be detectives together! Each number stands for a letter. How quickly can you find the word? Are you ready? Let’s go!”

Heads Up:

Heads Down:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - B Read and circle

details: Read and circle practices reading full sentences and choosing the correct feeling words by checking understanding of when to use -ing and -ed feeling words.
Look for accurate circling, neat pencil work, understanding when to use  -ing and -ed feeling words, and correct selection of words.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - Speaking Customer Survey (Step 1)

details: Complete the customer survey checks understanding and usage of the feeling words for different rides.
Look for neat writing, reading and saying the names of attractions and feeling words accurately and correctly, and choices that make sense.

“I’m going to write a review on the amusement park website. It was so much fun I want to tell everyone! Let’s all choose how we felt about each of the attractions. Maybe we all have different answers!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (closed pairs): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (open pairs): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Group discussion applies the sentence pattern ‘How was…? It was… I was…’ providing the chance to express  their feelings about  the attractions and sharing opinions and agree on feelings for each ride.
Look for clear questions and answers, correct use of ‘It was/I was’,  taking turns to ask and answer, and placing stickers on the rides that match the group’s chosen feelings.

“I want to take my friend to the amusement park. I’m going to tell them that the parade was boring, but the 3D film was exciting. And the petting zoo was scary - I was scared of the animals! Do you agree? Let’s find out what everyone thinks!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Sing): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
